discoveryHook.scenario: Molly Kate, treasurer of Gracie's Natural Superstore, visits Ipswich Bank to open a business checking account. The bank manager gives her a signature card and deposit slips. A checking account starts with these basic tools.

explanation: A [[kw:checking account]] allows a business or individual to deposit money and write checks (or use a debit card) to pay others.
A [[kw:signature card]] is a document the bank keeps on file with the account holder's authorized signature(s). It is used to verify the signature on checks.
A [[kw:deposit slip]] (or deposit ticket) lists the cash and checks being placed into the account. Preprinted deposit slips show the account number.
The bank provides a temporary checkbook until personalized checks arrive.

visuals.caption: Each item plays a critical role in establishing and using a checking account.

blocks.title: 2. Anatomy of a Check

explanation: A [[kw:check]] includes several fields: date, payee, numeric amount box, verbal amount line, signature line, memo line, and the MICR line at the bottom.
The [[kw:MICR line]] (Magnetic Ink Character Recognition) contains the routing number (identifies the bank), account number, and check number. This line is read by high‑speed sorting machines.
The [[kw:routing number]] (ABA number) is a 9‑digit code that specifies the financial institution. The [[kw:account number]] identifies the individual account.
The [[kw:check number]] appears in the upper‑right corner and also in the MICR line; it helps track checks.

formulaCard.formula: Routing Number (9 digits) ⏺ Account Number ⏺ Check Number
